newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bourse seen in 1320-1390 flag formation.
newsitem.headline: Greek bourse seen in 1320-1390 flag formation.

text.p: Greek shares have completed a 58 percent retracement hitting an intraday low at 1160 points on the benchmark index and will trade between 1320-1390, a flag formation, in the coming weeks said Eurobank's chief fund manager.

"The retracement was a severe correction. The market is giving retail investors who missed the boat the opportunity to renter the market," said Alex Pappas, general manager at Eurobank-Alico Fund Management.
"We'll be in a flag formation, trading between 1320 support and 1390 resistance in the next weeks."

The market will need news on March CPI inflation to break out of the flag. A lower inflation figure will push interest rates even lower and ignite another move to the upside with the market hitting new highs around 1450 points, he forecast.

But aside from the technical picture, Greek growth funds -- 120 billion drachmas -- presently make up only 1.7 percent of the Athens bourse's market capitalisation, a very low ratio compared to other markets, Pappas said.

"This ratio will rise, a result of asset reallocation into equities as investors search for better performance and reduce fixed income exposure," Pappas said. "We'll see the same thing that happened in other Mediterranean countries earlier."

Another key issue was also the reaction of investors who got in at the peak and suffered losses, scared by the market's volatility. They will realise that a strong base at around 1350 points will be formed.
"This will enhance sentiment and lead to a shift in their investment philosophy. They will adopt a longer term view," the fund manager said.

Greek shares which lost 17 percent in a sharp three-session correction came back with a surprising 6.53 percent bounce back on Wednesday. The benchmark index settled at 1292.17, up 79 points. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
